name: For Its Own Good
tagline: Everyone else keeps it going. You love it enough to end it.
epigraph: This glass's grape made one winemaker famous. Then he demoted his own famous wines.
glassware: a heavy old-fashioned glass, one large cube
language_row: Wren's resonance: ready on v2. Guest text 4-gram clean against every pour (Wren r4–r5; the stir reworded off lover-hero and hero-regular-guy). names_note: For Its Own Good (Wren; all three by r4–r5). In Support second, for Robin (Tomás's first pick, from Gaja's own "in support of Barbaresco"; cold, it reads "in support of what?"). Also considered: One Only, Taken Down a Rank.
open_items: The plan's lead, Steven Spurrier and the 1976 Paris tasting, failed Wren's point 2 and the person: he "thought I had it rigged for the French wines to win" (BusinessWeek 2001), called it a publicity exercise, and the idea was Patricia Gallagher's. The 2026 re-tasting (an Instagram post) and the 1988 award (not on the archived page) fell too. Darmagi is legend-grade and fails points 1 and 4.

Gaja's move had two reasons, both his: "in support of Barbaresco" (one Barbaresco only) and room for a little Barbera, for freshness, against the all-Nebbiolo rule (5% or 15%; sources disagree, so no figure). The crus' return from the 2013 vintage was his children's decision, "thanks also to the support of our father". One of the three wines' current labels checked (Sorì Tildìn).

The glass holds a young Langhe Nebbiolo in a syrup (warmed with sugar, never boiled), not Gaja's wine; chosen for price and reach, so the y4 coincidence clause is "as it happens". Grappa: young (giovane or bianco), 37.5–43%; no page calls grappa Piedmont's own ("a Piedmont grappa, if you can find one" is a style suggestion). The syrup's fridge life is Tomás's estimate.
The family's third Old-Fashioned; its glass is near Asked In's, the grappa base keeps the shape unique. Barbera is not in the glass (about 1 ml a drink).
